AGENDA
  PROPERTY MAINTENANCE AND BUILDING

Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Property Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation
Appeals Board (Board) on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter within its jurisdiction subject to
the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address the
Board, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to
the Secretary. The Board will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter
and prior to a vote. The Board will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral
Communications period.

 Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda,
 or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The Board may direct staff to investigate and/or
 schedule certain matters for consideration at a future Board meeting.

 Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Board:
  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the Board as a whole and not directed to individual Board members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a
City meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the Secretary’s office, (562) 929-5744. Assisted
listening devices are available at this meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire to use this device. Upon request,
the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to
persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed
will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the
meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Board regarding any item on this agenda after
it has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the Community Development Department, City Hall,
12700 Norwalk Boulevard during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday to Thursday and 8:00
a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5744. You may also contact the City Clerk via email
at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

   PROPERTY MAINTENANCE AND
  BUILDING REHABILITATION APPEALS BOARD
  SPECIAL MEETING
  JUNE 12, 2019

The meeting was called to order by Chair Apodaca at 7:00 p.m. in the Norwalk City Hall,
Council Chambers, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Present were Board
Members Collins, Juan, Lopez, Vice Chair Barragan, and Chair Apodaca. Also present
were Michael L. Garcia, Director of Community Development; Saeed Amirazizi, Building
and Safety Manager; Grissel Chavez, Director of Public Safety, Dolores Bustamante,
Senior Code Compliance Inspector; Gabriela Garcia, Management Analyst; and Ruth
Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

REORGANIZATION OF THE BOARD
The Board, by unanimous voice vote, appointed Rosa Barragan to serve as Chair for
the upcoming year and Scott D. Collins to serve as Vice Chair.

MEETING MINUTES
The Board approved the minutes of the Special Meeting of June 13, 2018.

DELINQUENT TRASH AND REFUSE COLLECTION ACCOUNTS
Report on delinquent trash accounts and the hearing of any objections of the
property owners liable for unpaid trash and refuse services in accordance with
the provisions of Chapter 8.48 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.

Chair Barragan opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Gabriela Garcia, Management
Analyst, presented a report stating that the City of Norwalk provides a mandatory
refuse service to protect the public health and welfare of its residents; that the refuse
haulers are authorized to pick up trash weekly, billing customers on a quarterly basis;
that the amount for services is due fifteen (15) days from the billing date; that on the
45th day from the beginning of each quarter a late fee is added if payment has not been
made; that the haulers make attempts during the year to collect on past-due accounts;
that, as authorized in the Municipal Code, the haulers are allowed to seek payment
through the tax rolls in June of each year for the period of April 1st of the previous year
through March 31st of the current year; that in May 2019, 3,095 notices were prepared
and mailed to all property owners with a delinquent balance as of March 31st by all
three waste haulers; that since the notices went out some delinquent accounts have
been paid; that payments will continue to be received through July 31st; that as of May
1st delinquent amounts totaled $257,219; that representatives from the trash companies
are available to answer any questions; and that staff recommends that the Board direct
staff to forward the listed properties to the City Council with a recommendation that the
delinquent properties be placed on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding balance
is paid prior to July 31, 2019.
 Minutes of the Special Meeting
Property Maintenance and

June 12, 2019

Since there were no persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Barragan closed the
public hearing.

It was moved by Vice Chair Collins and seconded by Board Member Juan to direct staff
to forward the listed properties to the City Council with a recommendation that the
delinquent properties be placed on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding balance
is paid prior to July 31, 2019.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Board Member Apodaca, Board Member Juan, Board Member Lopez,
  Vice Chair Collins and Chair Barragan
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

DELINQUENT WEEDS AND LITTER COLLECTION FEES
Report on the cost of abatement of weeds and litter and the hearing of any
objections of property owners liable to be assessed for such abatement in
accordance with the provisions of Chapter 8.28 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.

Chair Barragan opened the hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Director of Public Safety,
Grissel Chavez, stated that before the Board is the annual report on the cost of
abatement of weeds and litter for the work performed this past fiscal year, 2018/19;
that, as required, the property owner of a vacant property on Pontlavoy Avenue was
provided a notice of a Declaration of Substandard, which was also filed with the Los
Angeles County Recorder’s Office; that, as of this date, the property owner has not
responded; and that it is staff’s recommendation that the Board direct them to forward
the listed property to the City Council with a recommendation that the delinquent
amount of $1,298.45 be placed as a lien on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding
balance is paid prior to August 1, 2019.

Since there were no persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Barragan closed the
hearing.

It was moved by Vice Chair Collins and seconded by Board Member Juan to direct staff
to forward the listed property to the City Council with a recommendation that the
delinquent amount be placed as a lien on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding
balance is paid prior to August 1, 2019.

EMERGENCY BOARD-UP COSTS
Report on the cost of emergency board-ups and the hearing of any objections of
property owners liable to be assessed for such abatement in accordance with the
provisions of Chapter 15.32 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.

Chair Barragan opened the hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Director of Public Safety,
Grissel Chavez, stated that this is the annual report on the costs of emergency board-
ups performed by City staff and/or contractor for the 2018/19 and 2017/18 fiscal years
as required by the Municipal Code; that the property owners were noticed; that, as of
today, staff has not heard from any of the property owners; that the staff report includes
the 2017/18 amount of $9,578.15; that this was approved in June of 2018; however, the
required notice was not sent out; that with the Board’s approval this amount will be
placed for collection with the County Tax Roll after August 1, 2019; that the total
outstanding cost for the current year is $23,462.45; and that it is staff’s
recommendation that the Board direct staff to forward the listed properties to the City
Council with a recommendation that the delinquent amounts be placed as a lien on the
County Tax Roll unless the outstanding balance is paid prior to August 1, 2019.

Since there were no persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Barragan closed the
hearing.

It was moved by Vice Chair Collins and seconded by Board Member Juan to direct staff
to forward the listed properties to the City Council with a recommendation that the
delinquent amounts be placed as a lien on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding
balance is paid prior to August 1, 2019.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Board Member Apodaca, Board Member Juan, Board Member Lopez,
  Vice Chair Collins and Chair Barragan
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

APPEAL HEARING – CASE NO. 14050042
Norwalk Municipal Code violations on property located at Assessor’s Parcel No.
8078-010-018 (“Property”) Norwalk, California.

Chair Barragan opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Director of Public Safety,
Grissel Chavez, presented a report stating that this is an appeal for a vacant lot located
on the 10800 block of Hopland Street, Parcel No. 8078-010-018; that it is an
undeveloped lot measuring 10-feet wide by approximately 104-feet in depth located in
the Single-Family Residential (R-1) zone; that Code Compliance initiated a case based
on conditions on the property, such as overgrown grass and vegetation; that items kept
on the property consist of a boat and a trailer as well as an accumulation of other
miscellaneous trash and debris along with unapproved fencing, an animal cage and
other items of personal property; that based upon the condition of the property it was
declared a public nuisance on April 4, 2019 and that the property was ordered to be
vacated; that the owner was notified and the property was posted as shown on the
picture attached to the staff report; that on April 12, 2019, the property owner, Mr. Syed
Kaleem, submitted a written appeal request, which is attached to the staff report; that a
history of the property is also included in the staff report; that staff is recommending that
the Board adopt Resolution No. 19-01 allowing the Code Compliance Division to
continue to move forward, declaring the property a public nuisance, and ordering the
abatement of all substandard conditions. Further, she stated that the Code Inspector
assigned to this case, Angel Rivas, and Supervisor Dolores Bustamante are also in
attendance.

In response to Vice Chair Collins’ question if, at any time, the property owner submitted
plans for this property, Director Garcia stated that the applicant indicated that he intends
to submit plans for consideration by the Planning Commission. Planning Manager
Serrano added that Mr. Kaleem has requested an address for the property multiple
times, but has not submitted any construction drawings; and that staff has only seen
preliminary drawings for a single-family house.

The property owner, Syed Kaleem, stated that he has been talking to City officials in
regards to developing the property; that the debris shown in the picture is actually a
fence; that he placed the fence there so that his neighbor’s dog would not come onto his
property; that he has been cited before because his neighbor encroached and was
using the property; that when he acquired this property he told his neighbor to continue
using it; however, the City cited him for what his neighbor was doing; that he then put up
a fence which is not in good condition; that he noticed that there is a pipe on the
property; that, today, he e-mailed pictures to the Director who indicated that he did not
receive them; that his pictures show that he is maintaining his property in such a way

that from the public view the property does not constitute a nuisance; that the pipe is
located in the center of the property; that it goes from the school to the street; that the
pipe is 3-feet deep, approximately 6” wide and carries water; that the water gets
stagnant in the pipe and feeds vermin; that he went to the Norwalk-La Mirada Unified
School District requesting that they remove the pipe as he has a plan to develop the
property; that the School District sent him a letter indicating that they relinquished their
rights and that they closed the pipe from their end on April 28, 2019; that another 117-
feet of pipe needs to be removed; that he assumes the pipe is about fifty years old and
needs to be removed or replaced anyway; that the onus of responsibility lies on his
shoulders whether or not he uses the pipe; that he still needs permission from the City
and the School District to remove the pipe; that he will be continuing to pursue that; and
that, today, the City made it very clear to him that he does not need to apply for any
permits nor does he need any permission for that purpose.

In response to Ms. Chavez’ question if it is correct that he has been informed that he
does not need to apply for any permit to remove the pipe, Mr. Kaleem replied he is
referring to the portion of pipe on his property.

Vice Chair Collins commented on the pictures presented by staff, and he asked what is
Mr. Kaleem doing about cleaning up the site as this also helps create vermin.

Mr. Kaleem stated that regarding the wooden fence and material, he is going to remove
all that; that the neighbor has moved out; that, right now, that property is vacant and is
being renovated; and that the neighbors have agreed to put up a fence on their side.

In reply to Chair Barragan’s comment if the debris belongs to Mr. Kaleem, he answered
in the affirmative.

Vice Chair Collins stated that the violations started on April 28, 2014 and that it has
taken five years to get to this point.

Mr. Kaleem stated that this is not true; that there is a gap of about four years during
which the property was vacant; that the Code Enforcement activity started recently
where he was cited and pictures were taken; that he objected to the picture taking on
private property as it is not in public view; that Code Enforcement has a good point
regarding the debris, but that they should have approached him asking for permission to
take pictures.

Vice Chair Collins stated that Code Enforcement approached him by giving him
citations.

Mr. Kaleem stated that this is correct; however, unless he removes the pipe he cannot
take a step forward as he is trying to coordinate removal of everything at one time; that
he can request a re-hearing of this case or request delaying of the decision-making
process; and that, as he has to go back to the School District, he is not going to touch
the fence for now.

In response to Chair Barragan’s comment that the debris be removed, Mr. Kaleem
indicated that there is no debris, only the fence material. Vice Chair Collins asked what
about the boat and camper. Mr. Kaleem replied that he uses the boat to carry water as
there is no water on the property; that he planted flowers on the front to make the
property look nice; that he applied for water service and electrical service but was told
that they cannot move forward unless the City gives him an address, which he has
requested from the City; that he also requested the City to approve his plans based on
the fact that the property was developed in 1954; that it is the City’s position that the
property was developed after 1959 where some of the laws came in; and that those
laws, including the setback requirements, should not apply to his property.

Vice Chair Collins stated that he is sorry Mr. Kaleem is having trouble with the pipe,
address and water, but the bottom line is that the property needs to be cleaned up; and
that it has been a five-year saga to get to this point.

Ms. Chavez stated that over the course of the five years, multiple items have been
found; that they have come and gone; that the cases have started over again; that the
boat and trailer were removed at one point but they appeared again; that lots of different
items have been stored on the property from a refrigerator, sinks and various
miscellaneous items; that this is why over the course of five years the case has
continued with addressing the different conditions at that point in time; that with regards
to the court case that Mr. Kaleem is referring to, that was a result of an appeal of his
criminal conviction; that the Appellate Division of the Superior Court granted the case to
go back to trial, which was upon the request of Mr. Kaleem; that the Trial Judge was
supposed to take some action and schedule a trial within a thirty-day period; and that,
as the Court failed to do that, that case was dismissed due to a technicality on the
Court’s part.

In reply to Vice Chair Collins’ remark if Mr. Kaleem has any additional comments, Mr.
Kaleem indicated that if the Board is considering abatement, he would request that the
matter be postponed or delayed until such time as the pipe is removed.

In response to Board Member Apodaca’s question if Mr. Kaleem lives on the property,
he replied that he is staying there most of the time so that he can do the maintenance
work; that he had to get a court order as his neighbors partitioned half of his property
and dumped construction-related material on that half.

  6

In reply to Board Member Apodaca’s comment if it is correct that the neighbor is going
to build a fence, Mr. Kaleem answered in the affirmative. Further, he stated that on his
side he is planting a hedge which requires regular maintenance; and that once his plans
will be approved, there is going to be a brick wall.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Barragan closed
the public hearing.

It was moved by Vice Chair Collins and seconded by Board Member Juan to adopt
Resolution No. 19-01 declaring the Property at Assessor’s Parcel No. 8078-010-018 a
public nuisance, ordering the abatement of all substandard conditions.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE
AYES:  Board Member Apodaca, Board Member Juan, Board Member Lopez,
  Vice Chair Collins and Chair Barragan
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
There were no persons wishing to address the Board.

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 7:40 p.m.
